No. 151 is ambiguous in its reference to agricultural and horticul­ tural operations. Agricultural open burning is already protected by stat­ ute and can occur anytime throughout the year. It is important to note that the U ACC is currently analyzing the PM 10 problem,  but if open burning is not shown to contribute to PM10 nonattainment areas, the  committee has no intention of changing the current regulation. Finally, I have recently created a blue ribbon task force to look into air quality  issues. Until this task force completes it analysis and makes recommendations for  long term solutions to the Wasatch Front air quality problems, it is premature to  elimiate a piece of the possible solution. I therefore, am vetoing H.B. No. 151. Norman H. Bangerter  Governor
